scores.evidence: These are what everything else depends on, so they come first:
scores.rationale: Phases run discovery → foundations → skeleton → templates → gates/waves → progressive delivery, with explicit reasoning that canary needs trusted metrics; each is proven before the next.

scores.evidence: Build → unit tests → image → push → deploy to dev → promote to staging → manual approval → prod
scores.rationale: A real end-to-end prod skeleton exists but is Phase 2, after discovery and foundations, and observability is only minimal; it is not Phase 0.

scores.evidence: Make the core decisions: which CI engine, push-based deploys or GitOps (e.g. Argo CD), artifact registry, environment layout
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed up front, but with no defaults or flip conditions (only trunk-based is recommended).

scores.evidence: Business-critical or core services, now that the templates are proven
scores.rationale: Foundations-first and archetype grouping show some blast-radius thinking, but waves put low-risk services first and critical ones later, which is deliberate risk reduction rather than widest-impact first.

scores.evidence: Secrets management (Vault or a cloud secrets manager) and passwordless OIDC login from CI to the cloud
scores.rationale: Security is present in Phase 1 (secrets, OIDC) but the main gates are in Phase 4; Phases 2, 3 and 5 don't show concrete security work.

scores.evidence: Deploys show up as events in your observability tool
scores.rationale: Observability first appears in Phase 2, not in Foundations, and later phases mention it only in part (SLO metrics, DORA dashboards).

scores.evidence: The platform's own infrastructure defined as code, so it can be rebuilt
scores.rationale: IaC, versioned templates and charts give reproducibility in Phases 1 and 3, but it isn't treated in every phase, and nothing covers pinned builds.

scores.evidence: Rollback works and has been tested on purpose
scores.rationale: Rollback appears in Phase 2, the scorecard and Phase 6, but not in Foundations, and runner failure or HA is not covered.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, and the request is a non-AI system, so there is no N/A declaration.

scores.evidence: This comes late on purpose. Canary analysis needs metrics you can trust and a standardized deploy path
scores.rationale: Deferred items (progressive delivery, optimization, long-tail services) are placed later with some reasons, but there is no explicit not-built list with pull-forward conditions.

note: Solid, pragmatic sequence with good dependency ordering and a real skeleton. It lacks default/flip decision gates, observability from Phase 0, security and resilience threaded through every phase, and an explicit AI-N/A statement.
